rules: Attempt all constructions in 8 columns, with column 0 blank; four staves may occupy columns 1, 3, 5, 7.
Use native dotless-i heads and feet on standalone uprights; use contextual native n/m/u terminals on connected staves.
Match the Quintessential part order and spine handedness; do not rotate a complete glyph cell to construct a turned form.
A long bowl closes only against its declared immediate straight neighbor, including implicit extensions omitted from the name.
Straight and curved extensions must remain distinct. Keep each quartet's body fixed outside explicit extension and contact pixels.
Use 8-neighbor ink and 4-neighbor white connectivity. A topology flag requests inspection; it does not erase a legitimate donor feature.
Native Latin terminal shapes govern each context: preserve exact donor details and do not add decorative bulbs, serifs or stroke thickening from the outline design.

Use exact native a for spine with stem and exact native turned a for stem with spine. Shared spines combine turned-a upper connections with upright-a lower connections and a thin coordinated waist, balancing the body before adding extensions.
The narrow central spine crossover is at row 9, as directed in the foundation feedback.
This batch completes forms without middle components. Further descendants require individual drawing and visual inspection.
